title: Rebase and re-verify a verified job whose base moved on main
summary: When a verified job is Stale because its base is no longer an ancestor of main (e.g. after a revert) or main moved in governed content, Athena gains a path (reached via `athena go <job>` on the stale job, like the existing blocked-job retry) that rebases the candidate onto the current tip, re-verifies it, and lands it. Audience: the Athena operator, who today copies verified work by hand. A test shows a verified job whose base moved is rebased and re-verified, not left Stale.

defaults_applied.how: New tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Test asserts a Landed outcome after rebase and re-verification, not just wiring.
Behavior criteria name cargo test as the check.
Docs and changelog written for an outside reader.
One focused path, reusing retry_landing and plan().
Handles any base movement (revert, rewrite), not only one case.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The entry point is `athena go <job>` on a job whose outcome is Stale, mirroring retry_landing for Blocked jobs in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs; no new subcommand.
Rebase means replaying the candidate's diff over the new tip (git merge-tree style, as plan() already does for records-only changes); a conflict leaves the job Stale with a clear reason.
Re-verification runs the normal verifier on the rebased candidate; landing only follows a passing new verification, never the old one.
plan() in land.rs keeps its current Stale rules; the rebase path is layered on top, so unrelated stale cases (exclusion rule changes) are not silently bypassed.
Test uses the existing test harness in athena-core or athena-cli/tests (lifecycle.rs, drain.rs style), with a scripted verifier.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test builds a verified job, moves main so the job's base is no longer an ancestor (e.g. a revert or rewritten history), runs the rebase path, and asserts the job gets a new candidate on the new tip, a fresh verification, and a Landed outcome rather than staying Stale. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows a rebase that conflicts with the moved main leaves the job Stale with a reason naming the conflict and lands nothing. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows that if re-verification of the rebased candidate fails, nothing lands and the failure is recorded; the old verification is never reused for the new content. Run `cargo test`.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
CHANGELOG.md and any CLI help describe how an operator rebases a stale verified job (what command, what happens on conflict), readable by an outside reader.

Existing landing tests (a_verified_candidate_lands_on_its_base, landing_refuses_content_that_differs_from_the_verified_content) still pass unchanged, so the landing gate still refuses unverified content.

out_of_scope: Automatically rebasing every stale job without operator action
Changing the landing gate or the exclusion-rule staleness checks
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
Rebasing jobs that were never verified
departures: Touches landing and verification flow in a large module with git-state tests, so cost and time are above the reference median.
hard_reason: Changes how verified work lands and when re-verification is required, so a mistake could land unverified content.
